theme: Source-qualified complete dictionary extraction and conservative morphology candidates
question: Can general source-backed extraction repairs preserve the complete Winslow population and expose unresolved morphology for a fair later reading comparison?
outcome: Re-extracted 69310 Winslow records from 978 pages. Selected two-member rows changed from 18426 to 25653; 8138 member lists changed. Lexicon assistance, parent borrowing marks and unresolved increment candidates have separate provenance. All comparative-scorer eligibility remains false. No rebus effect or real confirmation was run. Parent code review found inherited vowel-length folding in increment generation beyond the exact-match scope. A preserved-run audit flags 2 of 59 analyses on 2 rows; the exact subset retains 57 unresolved analyses on all 57 candidate-bearing rows. Five audit tests and separate exact-count/hash replay pass.
challenge: Printed boundaries and lexical senses are distinct. Lexicon-assisted Winslow rows create comparative source dependence; borrowed parents, morphological increments and historical senses require specialist review. The initial report incorrectly restricted inherited e/ē and o/ō folding to cross-dictionary alignment; the candidate-layer deviation is now quantified separately.
remedy: Pinned protocol, imported parents, complete tables and all source pages; retained original and guarded members, exact-headword cross-source evidence, unresolved candidates and separate known-regression checks.
retry_when: Independent Tamil specialist review resolves remaining morphology, senses and lexical eligibility; a later calibrated comparison declares dictionary dependence and freezes all participants before reviewed unexamined confirmation.
